answer: Each epoch, work is graded by a panel drawn by verifiable random lottery, so no agent knows its judges in advance and panels never repeat. To rig a verdict an attacker must bribe the randomly chosen jurors before results publish, and each juror posts a stake slashed if the panel is proven collusive. Rigging becomes a recurring gamble whose cost scales with panel size every epoch: like crossing a bridge into a lagoon whose guards are redrawn each crossing, so a sable network of fake identities earns nothing beyond honest fees.
